themes.theme: Whether EMOM and AMRAP count as HIIT, and whether the answer changes how you set the timer
themes.hook: CrossFit vocabulary and HIIT vocabulary grew up separately, so people arrive genuinely unsure whether the EMOM they just did was cardio, conditioning, or something else entirely.
themes.evidence: Google already puts this site on the front page for the exact phrasing people use, at position 7-8, and the existing formats post never answers the category question they are asking.
pain_quotes: Cannot tell whether an EMOM counts toward their weekly HIIT target.
Assumes AMRAP and HIIT are the same thing and then wonders why the intensity feels different.
Wants to know whether the work-to-rest ratio changes when a session is called one thing or the other.
themes.distinctFrom: hiit-methods-comparison (0.36) compares HIIT, HIIS, Tabata and SIT and never mentions EMOM or AMRAP at all; amrap-emom-tabata-hiit-formats-compared (0.31) compares those three formats to each other but assumes you already accept they are all HIIT. This post answers the prior question — is it — and what that means for the timer.
themes.searchEvidence: Striking distance: 'amrap vs hiit' 21 impressions at position 7.0, 'emom vs hiit' 17 impressions at position 8.3, both zero clicks (90 days).
themes.imagePrompt: Two people working through a circuit in a bright box gym, one mid kettlebell swing and one hands on hips recovering, rubber flooring, open roller door behind

themes.theme: Running a full interval session from the Watch with the iPhone left at home
themes.hook: The whole point of a wrist timer is not carrying the phone, and the moment you actually leave it behind you find out which parts of your setup quietly depended on it.
themes.query: interval timer on apple watch without phone
themes.evidence: Search Console shows steady impressions on standalone Apple Watch timer phrasing at positions in the teens and thirties, and r/crossfit threads specifically ask for a wrist timer so they can leave the phone in the bag.
pain_quotes: Leaves the phone in a locker and finds the workout will not start on the Watch alone.
Wants audio or haptic cues without carrying a phone for the speaker.
Is unsure whether a workout built on the phone is already saved on the wrist or needs a sync first.
themes.distinctFrom: best-apple-watch-interval-timer (0.44) is a buying guide answering which app to install; this post assumes Peak Interval is already installed and answers the capability question — what a standalone Watch session can and cannot do once the iPhone is out of range, and what to set up before you leave it behind.
themes.searchEvidence: Striking distance: 'interval timer on apple watch' 2 impressions at position 38.5, 'interval training on apple watch' at position 15, 'workout timer apple watch' at position 33 (90 days).
themes.imagePrompt: A runner pausing at the top of a coastal path at dawn, wrist raised across the chest, no phone or armband anywhere, sea haze behind, low warm light

themes.theme: Whether a physical gym wall timer is worth buying when your phone and watch already do it
themes.hook: A wall timer is a few hundred pounds of hardware doing something the device in your pocket already does — the case for it is real but much narrower than the people selling them suggest.
themes.evidence: An r/crossfit thread asking whether people training alone use a phone timer or buy a real one drew nearly thirty replies, and separate threads hunt for reviews of specific wall-timer hardware.
pain_quotes: Is about to spend real money on hardware and cannot tell what it buys over a free app.
Trains alone in a garage and wants a clock readable from across the room mid-set.
Is tired of unlocking a phone with chalky hands between rounds.
themes.distinctFrom: apple-watch-workout-app-intervals-vs-timer-app (0.22) weighs the stock watchOS Workout app against a dedicated timer app, both software on a device you already own; this post is a hardware purchase decision — a wall-mounted gym clock against the phone or watch — where visibility across a room and shared use by more than one person are the only arguments that hold up.
themes.searchEvidence: Keyword research: 'gym timer' 880/mo, 'crossfit gym timer' 480/mo MEDIUM competition.
themes.imagePrompt: A garage gym seen from the doorway with a rig, plates and a rower, one athlete resting between rounds looking toward the far wall, morning light across the concrete

themes.theme: Interval timers without a subscription: what the free tiers actually take away
themes.hook: Almost every timer in the store is free to install, and almost every one of them puts something you need behind a monthly charge — the trick is knowing which limits you will hit in week two.
themes.evidence: Requests for a timer with no subscription, no ads and a one-off price are one of the most repeated asks in r/hiit and r/crossfit, and are the stated reason several people gave for building their own app instead.
pain_quotes: Is happy to pay once and refuses to pay monthly for a countdown.
Hits a three-saved-workouts cap the moment they build a real training week.
Finds the ad appears exactly at the round change, when the screen mattered.
themes.distinctFrom: best-tabata-timer (0.28) asks which app runs 20/10 intervals best and treats price as a footnote; this post is the pricing question on its own — subscription versus one-off versus ad-supported, which limits free tiers actually impose (saved workout caps, Watch access, custom cues), and how to tell before you install.
themes.searchEvidence: Keyword research: 'free interval timer' 260/mo, 'free workout timer' 90/mo; supported by repeated no-subscription phrasing in the pain signals.
themes.imagePrompt: Close overhead of a phone face down on a gym bench next to a water bottle and a wrapped skipping rope, worn wooden bench, soft window light

themes.theme: Building one session where some rounds are counted in reps and others in seconds
themes.hook: Real training is rarely all clock or all reps — fifty squats then a sixty-second plank then ten push-ups — and almost every timer forces you to pick one and fake the other.
themes.query: interval timer for reps and time
themes.evidence: An r/hiit thread laid out exactly this structure round by round and asked whether any app supports it; the replies were mostly other people saying they wanted the same thing.
pain_quotes: Wants a stopwatch for the rep rounds and a countdown for the timed ones, in one workout.
Guesses at how long a rep block will take and ends up standing around or cut short.
Gives up and runs two apps side by side, then loses the place in both.
themes.distinctFrom: timer-vs-rep-based-hiit (0.16) argues which of the two approaches suits your goals and treats hybrids as a concept; this post skips the argument and answers the build question — how to lay out a single session that alternates counted rounds and timed rounds, including how to size a rep block so the timer stays honest.
themes.searchEvidence: Pain-signal theme; keyword check returned no volume for the exact phrasing, which the tool documents as unreliable rather than evidence of no demand.
themes.imagePrompt: A person kneeling on a mat between exercises in a living room, resistance band and a single kettlebell nearby, sofa pushed back against the wall, evening lamp light
